### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **2** package(s): `@objectstack/plugin-auth`, `@objectstack/spec`, touching **50** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **2** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/spec/api-surface/contracts.json`, `packages/spec/export-origins/contracts.json`), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**48** hand-written doc(s) name something this change touched — list omitted above 15 rows. Re-derive on the tree named below: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 0a168a33ea06b92e1e6f45bc38e2cd20b665d6a1`.

⛔ **12** release-owned page(s) also affected — read-only, see AGENTS.md Documentation Guardrails.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **2** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/spec/api-surface/contracts.json`, `packages/spec/export-origins/contracts.json`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **2** anchor(s) matched too much of the corpus to be a work list: `PERMISSION_DENIED (literal, 36 pages)`, `sys_user (literal, 41 pages)`
- **13** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **54** of **206** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **146** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 0a168a33ea06b92e1e6f45bc38e2cd20b665d6a1` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `bdee5d38afb5fdaa9b92ece59190952c2dc12ac5` — the merge of head `53e173d2a79755eadcead2145dbb82bd236e7673` into base `0a168a33ea06b92e1e6f45bc38e2cd20b665d6a1`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin bdee5d38afb5fdaa9b92ece59190952c2dc12ac5 && git checkout bdee5d38afb5fdaa9b92ece59190952c2dc12ac5
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 0a168a33ea06b92e1e6f45bc38e2cd20b665d6a1 53e173d2a79755eadcead2145dbb82bd236e7673 && git checkout -B drift-repro 0a168a33ea06b92e1e6f45bc38e2cd20b665d6a1 && git merge --no-ff 53e173d2a79755eadcead2145dbb82bd236e7673

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 0a168a33ea06b92e1e6f45bc38e2cd20b665d6a1
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 0a168a33ea06b92e1e6f45bc38e2cd20b665d6a1` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## 席位核对 · ACCEPT · PR #23786 @ `53e173d2a7` (#23772) · `domain:spec` seat 1 · `os-elon-musk` · session `session_01HjR8RUwTPQ3TgbfKihmxp9` · 2026-10-16T02:22Z

Reviewer of record. Every item below was checked against GitHub, not against the report (`6206536077` on #23772).

- **Shape:**
  - Draft, base `main`. The first line is `Fixes #23772`, the body's only closing keyword, then `Clause-②: yes`, matching claim `6205711728` and the changeset.
  - 12 files, +964/−2, none governed (`check-governed-merges`: 0 of 12 paths, 966 lines ≤ 3000). Assignee `os-elon-musk`.
- **The governing rulings, read in the diff:**
  - **#22269 OQ1 A:** `mintPrincipalSession?` is an OPTIONAL `IAuthService` member, so every existing implementation compiles. Its types (`PrincipalSession`, `PrincipalSessionCookie`, `PrincipalSessionMintOptions`) and `PRINCIPAL_SESSION_MAX_TTL_SECONDS = 120` sit in `contracts/auth-service.ts`. `AuthManager.mintPrincipalSession` delegates to `principal-session-mint.ts`. In-process only, and no route is added.
  - **#22269 OQ9 A, refused before any mint:**
    - no user, `isSystem`, or a `principalKind` other than `human`: `PERMISSION_DENIED` / `403`;
    - the user row missing, not a human (`isHumanUserRow`), or banned with `banExpires` honoured: `PERMISSION_DENIED` / `403`;
    - an `authGate` carried on the context, or resolved live for the context's `tenantId`: `403` with the posture's own code via `judgeHeldSession`;
    - `ttlSeconds` outside 1..120 or not an integer: `VALIDATION_ERROR` / `400`, refused and never clamped.
  - **#8346 B′ M2, "no system principal":** the session is the caller's own (`impersonatedBy` unset, the active organization = `tenantId`).
- **The card's pins:**
  - **Never renewed, on both lanes:** one `session.update.before` guard, composed after the host's hook (a host `false` still aborts), clamps a branded session's `expiresAt` to its minted ceiling. It covers the cookie lane, the bearer lane over HTTP and the in-process bearer read. Each lane file carries a control: an unbranded 120 s session IS renewed by the same read.
  - **Ablation:** neutralising the guard reds exactly the three lane pins (3 failed / 24 passed). The restore is byte-identical.
  - **Revoke:** bound to the minted token and idempotent. After it, neither the token nor the cookie resolves, over HTTP and in-process.
  - **The cookie:** better-auth's own `authCookies.sessionToken` name and attributes, so `cookiePrefix` and `__Secure-` follow the deployment.
  - **The brand:** `psm_` is server-written, with 32 random characters after it. A client cannot mint a branded token, and a spoofed prefix could only stop its own session's renewal.
- **Outside the claimed file surface, accepted:**
  - `content/docs/permissions/system-context.mdx` row 61b. The derived `check-system-context-census` requires a row for the new `isSystem` refusal site; it first exited 1 and was re-run to 0.
  - The shared test fixture `principal-session-mint-test-support.ts` (the `audience-gate-test-support.ts` precedent).
- **The report's open questions, the seat's calls:** all A.
  - An API-key context may mint: ADR-0090 D10 makes a key its owner's credential, and B would widen `ExecutionContext` without a pull.
  - The fixed 120 s ceiling, refused above.
  - The token brand over a `sys_session` column: no schema change, and every node agrees.
  - The line count: the true figure is +964/−2 (966). The body's 965 predates the census row. The excess over the card's 560–640 estimate is pins and the module's measured-trap header.
- **Carried to #22269, the consumer (Acceptance notes, no producer here):**
  - Each mint fires the existing `session.create.after` audit writer, so a render leaves a login row.
  - `ExecutionContext` carries no impersonation marker. A mint made while an admin impersonates the user is therefore logged as the user's own session, with no `impersonated_by`. Whether a render under impersonation mints at all, or how it is attributed, is the consumer's call at its door.
- **Changeset:** `@objectstack/spec` and `@objectstack/plugin-auth`, both `minor`, `Clause-②: yes (widening)`. The sentences were checked against the code: every refusal and its code, "refused, never clamped", the cookie attributes, and the revoke contract.
- **Before the queue:** a `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER` contract review (face `packages/spec/src/contracts/**`, and the widening `Clause-②: yes` declares), and every check green on the head. #22269 lands after this one.

Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/spec/src/contracts/auth-service.ts + packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/principal-session-mint.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/auth-manager.ts (`composeDatabaseHooks`'s new `session.update.before`, `AuthManager.mintPrincipalSession`), packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/principal-session-mint.test.ts, principal-session-mint.cookie-lane.pin.test.ts, principal-session-mint.bearer-lane.pin.test.ts and principal-session-mint-test-support.ts, packages/spec/src/contracts/auth-service.test.ts, .changeset/23772-principal-session-mint.md, packages/spec/api-surface/contracts.json, packages/spec/export-origins/contracts.json, content/docs/permissions/system-context.mdx (row 61b); and, because every guarantee the contract states is a claim about the pinned dependency, better-auth 1.7.3 as the PR head declares it (`packages/plugins/plugin-auth/package.json`), read as files out of the pnpm content store, never installed, built or run: `dist/api/routes/session.mjs`, `dist/api/routes/update-session.mjs`, `dist/db/with-hooks.mjs`, `dist/db/internal-adapter.mjs`, `dist/plugins/bearer/index.mjs`, `dist/context/create-context.mjs`, and `@better-auth/core` 1.7.3 `dist/utils/id.mjs`.

Inputs: card #23772 (body and all three comments), PR #23786 (body, 12-file list, net diff against `main` at the head: +964 / -2), and the check-runs on the head. Read-only throughout: the branch was fetched, nothing was checked out, built, tested or re-run.

### ① Derived judgments

Public-surface changes the diff implies, each judged:

1. **`IAuthService.mintPrincipalSession?(context, options?)` — an optional member.** Right. No class in `packages/` declares `implements IAuthService` (re-grepped at the head); the readers that name the type take an optional member unchanged. The spec test pins that a minimal implementation still satisfies the contract, and `principal-session-mint.test.ts` pins that `AuthManager`'s method is assignable to the member's own type, so the two cannot drift.
2. **Four new exports from `@objectstack/spec/contracts`:** `PRINCIPAL_SESSION_MAX_TTL_SECONDS` (a constant, 120), `PrincipalSession`, `PrincipalSessionCookie`, `PrincipalSessionMintOptions`. Right. The `api-surface` and `export-origins` shards add exactly those four and remove nothing, matching the hunks; a constant carries no logic, so Prime Directive #2 holds.
3. **`AuthManager.mintPrincipalSession` becomes public** (`AuthManager` is re-exported by the package index). Right, and deliberately narrow: `principal-session-mint.ts` is not re-exported, so `PrincipalSessionMintRefusalError`, `holdPrincipalSessionExpiry` and the `psm_` brand stay package-internal and a consumer reads a refusal by its `code` and `status` alone, as the contract text says.
4. **One `session.update.before` database hook on every session.** Right. For a session without the brand the guard returns `undefined` and the write is byte-identical to before; a host hook chains first, its `false` aborts, its `{ data }` is merged exactly as better-auth's own loop merges (`with-hooks.mjs:55-58`), and the host's `update.after` is kept.
5. **No accept-set change.** Right: no Zod schema, no authorable key, no HTTP route, no env var, no impersonation path (`admin-impersonate-endpoint.ts` and `impersonation-bearer-rotation.ts` are not in the file list). Row 61b on the system-context register is the census gate's requirement for the new `isSystem` refusal site. Right.

Each guarantee the contract states, judged against the implementation and the pinned better-auth:

- **The refusals, all before any mint.** `refuseUpFront` runs before the auth context is even fetched: no `userId`, `isSystem`, or a `principalKind` other than `human` (the enum is exactly `human | agent | service | guest | system`, `execution-context.zod.ts:181`, absent reads as `human`) answer `PERMISSION_DENIED` / 403; a `ttlSeconds` that is not an integer in 1..120 answers `VALIDATION_ERROR` / 400; a carried `authGate` answers 403 with the posture's own code through `judgeHeldSession`, the same judge the platform-admin surface uses. Then the row: missing, not `isHumanUserRow` (the one predicate the audience gate and the dev seed read), or banned without a lapsed `banExpires`, answer 403; then the posture computed now, `resolveUserAuthGates(userId, { organizationId: tenantId })`, answers 403 with its code. `createSession` is reached only after all five. Right. Every refusal is pinned with the envelope and with "createSession never called, no `sys_session` row appeared", and each of the four non-human kinds is pinned separately.
- **The TTL ceiling.** `expiresAt = now + ttl` seconds, written through `createSession(userId, false, { token, expiresAt, activeOrganizationId }, true)`. In 1.7.3 the adapter's defaults for `expiresAt` and `token` are spread before `...overrideAll ? rest : {}` (`internal-adapter.mjs:261-277`), so the short life holds only with `overrideAll`, and the mint passes `true`. An ask above 120, below 1, fractional or `NaN` is refused, never clamped. Right. If the store returned a different token the stray would be deleted and `INTERNAL_ERROR` / 500 thrown. Right.
- **Never renewed by a read on either lane.** Verified against the 1.7.3 source, not the PR body. The only writers that raise a session's `expiresAt` in the whole dist are `get-session` (`session.mjs:199-202`); `update-session.mjs:37` writes only the additional fields `parseSessionInput` admits plus `updatedAt`, and the organization plugin writes `activeOrganizationId` / `activeTeamId` only. `internalAdapter.updateSession(token, data)` takes no context argument: `updateWithHooks` (`with-hooks.mjs:43-60`) fetches the endpoint context from async-local storage (`tryGetCurrentAuthEndpointContext`), runs `session.update.before` with `(data, context)` before the database write and before the secondary-storage custom function alike, and merges a returned `{ data }` into what is written. `get-session` sets `ctx.context.session` to the session it found (`session.mjs:154`) before the renewal write, and `sessionMiddleware` sets it (`:274`) for `update-session`, so for every caller in 1.7.3 the session on the context IS the session being updated, which is the guard's one assumption. The brand is read off the stored token; `generateId` draws from `a-z A-Z 0-9` only (`@better-auth/core` `utils/id.mjs`), so a random token can never start with `psm_`, and no client can write a token onto a row. Right. Pinned on the cookie lane, the bearer lane over HTTP and the in-process bearer read (the one lane `inProcessSessionReadInput` cannot shield, since `disableRefresh` rides only a cookie request), each file with a control proving the same fixture renews an unbranded 120-second session. The dev's one-shot ablation of the guard call reddened exactly those three pins; reported, not re-run here.
- **The revoke.** `deleteSession(rawToken)`, bound to the one minted token; the `revoked` latch is set only after the delete returns, so a failed delete is retryable and a second call is a no-op. Under secondary storage `deleteSession` removes the key entry too (`internal-adapter.mjs:451` onward). Pinned: afterwards both HTTP lanes answer 401 `UNAUTHENTICATED` and the in-process read answers `null`. Right.
- **The cookie attributes.** Name and attributes are `authContext.authCookies.sessionToken`, better-auth's derivation from the `advanced.cookiePrefix` / `useSecureCookies` that `AuthManager` passes; nothing restated. Pinned: `better-auth.session_token` not Secure on http; `__Secure-acme.session_token`, Secure and HttpOnly under prefix `acme`, and that cookie authenticates. The value is better-call's signed form, which the bearer plugin takes as already signed when it contains a dot and HMAC-verifies (`bearer/index.mjs:34-40`), so one value serves both lanes. Right.
- **The active organization.** The context's `tenantId` is copied onto the session; `defaultActiveOrg` keeps a present override. No membership check is made at the mint: the context is server-constructed and its `tenantId` came from the user's own admitted session or key. Right under the platform's existing context trust; named under ③.

Adversarial paths looked for, each closed:

- *Mint for someone other than the caller.* Only by constructing an `ExecutionContext` that names another user, which is the same in-process trust every data-engine call already extends; there is no HTTP door, and the one context that legitimately names any user, `isSystem`, is refused.
- *A session outliving its ceiling.* The renewal is the only raise and is pinned on the write; `AuthManager` drops `session.cookieCache` by construction (its own comment block), so no cached answer outlives a revoke; `get-session` deletes an expired row on sight (`session.mjs:153-163`). After a pinned renewal better-auth re-sets the session cookie with a 7-day `Max-Age`: a carrier attribute only, the row still ends at the ceiling.
- *A refusal bypassed.* `Number.isInteger` refuses strings and `NaN`; an undeclared `principalKind` cannot be built from the Zod schema; a lapsed ban mints, which is what better-auth's own sign-in does.
- *The guard harming another session.* It acts only when the context's session is branded and the update raises `expiresAt` above the stored value, and every 1.7.3 caller updates the context's own session, so it can never pin a different session's expiry.

### ② Semver level

`.changeset/23772-principal-session-mint.md`: `@objectstack/spec` minor, `@objectstack/plugin-auth` minor. Both packages publish (`private` unset, 18.0.0-next.1). The PR body declares `Clause-②: yes`; the changeset carries `Clause-②: yes (widening)`, one arm from the closed pair, and `yes` takes at least `minor`: met. Nothing is removed or renamed, so no migration text and no ADR-0087 disposition is owed. `Check Changeset` is green on the head. Right. No `skip-changeset` label, correctly.

### ③ Boundary flags

The dev's open questions, answered:

1. *An API-key-authenticated context can mint; keep (A) or refuse keys (B)?* **A, answered.** Measured at the head: `resolve-authz-context.ts:530-536` resolves a key as its owner and ADDS the key's `scopes` to the owner's permissions as a seed, never subtracts, so a key-admitted context is at least the owner's reach and a minted session (the owner's plain session) never exceeds its key. `ResolvedAuthzContext.credential` exists at the authz layer but is not assembled onto `ExecutionContext`, so B is a spec widening with no pull. ADR-0090 D10 holds as the dev read it.
2. *TTL: a fixed 120-second ceiling, refused above, default equal to the ceiling.* **A, answered.** A constant in spec is within Prime Directive #2; refuse-over-clamp is Prime Directive #12's direction; a setting without a named deployment is scope.
3. *A token brand rather than a `sys_session` column.* **A, answered.** The alphabet proof above makes the brand unforgeable by chance, and only the server writes tokens.
4. *Line budget 966 against 560-640; body says 965.* **A, answered.** The excess is the three pin files and their fixture (about 480 lines) plus the module header; the body figure predates the one-line docs commit. Note only.

The dev's deviations: row 61b is the census gate's requirement, right; the test-only fixture is imported by nothing in the package and not re-exported, right; the gates ran on the merge head `e3db58a8` with the docs-only commit's families re-run on the final head, and the check-runs on the final head are the verdicts, right; the six commits carry exactly the session-URL and co-author trailer pair AGENTS.md prescribes (its line 461), right.

The dev's observations, confirmed: a mint fires the `session.create.after` login audit writer (and a revoke fires the `session.delete.after` logout writer) with no endpoint path, carried to #22269 by the lane ACCEPT, the right carrier; `enforceConcurrentCap` runs only in the `/sign-in/email` after-hook (`auth-manager.ts:2640`), so a mint never evicts a session and only a sign-in inside the 120 seconds counts it; the `Failed to find admin session` line predates the PR.

Escalated, none blocking:

- **Impersonation attribution.** `ExecutionContext` carries no impersonation marker (none in the spec kernel, core, runtime or types at the head), so a mint from an admin's impersonation session is a session for the impersonated user with `impersonatedBy` unset and a login audit row naming the user alone: equal reach to what the admin already holds, at most 120 seconds, but the ADR-0118 attribution is dropped for that window. The lane ACCEPT carried this to #22269; the consumer cannot tell either, so the fix shape is a server-set marker on the context, a spec widening read by the mint. That is a maintainer decision outside this card's pins (the card excludes the impersonation paths) and is named here for one.
- **The in-process trust boundary.** The member mints for whatever `userId` the context names. That is the platform's standing context trust, and the contract text says "the requesting user's execution context"; #22269's review should hold its consumer to handing over the request's own context and never one it assembles.
- **The dependency pin.** The non-extension rests on two facts of better-auth 1.7.3: the hook receives the endpoint context through async-local storage, and every `updateSession` caller targets the context's own session. A better-auth bump must re-read `session.mjs`, `update-session.mjs` and `with-hooks.mjs`; the three lane pins run real better-auth and are the tripwire.

Check-runs on the head, all completed before this record was posted: 36 success, 5 skipped (opt-in gates and matrix placeholders), no failure; the six Test Core shards, both Type Check jobs, Check Changeset, Spec property liveness and the Governed Surface Queue Guard are among the green. Those conclusions are the gate verdicts; nothing was re-run here.
